answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with stake-backed identity: each agent locks a bond of copper to earn one voting key, so a thousand fake personas require a thousand bonds. Peers check that each key traces to a distinct funding source, and any key caught double-voting near a reef of lookalike addresses is slashed, burning its bond. Honest agents keep their stake and earn fees from the inlet of real trade, while an attacker pays a rising, unrecoverable cost for every alias, making a flood of identities economically irrational long before it can swing a vote.
